title: Worker hello
description: The body of POST /api/station/stt/hello, as the GPU worker client sends it today (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py hello; read by WorkerApi.handle, sizeup/cloud/sttworkers.py). JSON with a Content-Length, at most 1 MiB. The hub resolves the bearer token first: a GPU worker's own (sw1.<id>.<secret>), or a station's token for its whisper, which the hub knows as `station:<id>` and takes only while that station's whisper is in the pool. Sent once when the worker connects, and again after the hub was away.

build.description: The release tag of the build that runs ("" when the worker can't tell: a folder unpacked by hand).

state.description: The update in words: ok, downloading b12728, b12728: waiting (gaming), b12728 ready, waiting: a clip, switching to b12728, rolled back: <why> (again in 30 min), bad: <why>, not managed (own path), off (auto_update), ... The hub keeps 60 characters.

worker.description: The id the worker believes it has. The hub does not read it: the id is the token's.

state.description: `online`, `gaming` (the machine is in use: no jobs) or `paused`. The hub ignores a word it does not know and keeps the state it had.

model.description: The speech-to-text model's name. The hub keeps 80 characters.

version.description: The worker client's version. The hub keeps 40 characters.

gpu.title: GPU
gpu.description: The graphics card as nvidia-smi gives it. The hub keeps only these keys, each a number or a string.

name.description: The card's name. The hub keeps it; today's worker client does not send it.

load.title: Load
load.description: A station's whisper only: its own work and pace. The hub keeps only these keys, each a number or a string.

own.description: Clips of the station's own being transcribed now.

rtf.description: Its measured pace: seconds of decoding per second of audio.

max_s.description: The longest clip it would take, seconds of audio. The hub never offers it a longer one.

why.description: With `paused`: why it is not claiming now.

models.title: Models
models.description: The models the worker serves. The hub reads it on every request (sizeup/cloud/infer.py seen); a key left out is unchanged. The worker client in tools/stt_worker sends it in every hello and state post.

llm.description: The language model; "" for none now.

stt_try.description: The try (challenger) ids whose try server answers now: a try model's own, or a separate try instance of a model this worker also serves live (its primary, a wanted one), each having passed its test decode and not being unloaded (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py Models.try_ready). Sent only to a hub that names a catalog. The claim body carries the same list as `try_loaded`: a challenger job only for an id in it.

keep_awake.title: Keep awake
keep_awake.description: A GPU worker on Windows (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py KeepAwake): whether it keeps the PC from idle sleep. Left out off Windows and by a worker from before. Health shows "keeps PC awake" while held, and "offline since HH:MM (asleep?)" on a GPU worker gone silent (unheard 30 s, not after a clean stop: reason `shutdown`) whose last word said off or not held, or whose last state was `online` (its heartbeats just stopped, with no pause or gaming first): sizeup/sttpool.py Pool.asleep. A hub from before ignores it.

held.description: The flag is set now: false while paused by hand, before the worker's first tick, or when Windows refused it.

why.description: Not held: why, in words (starting, paused, refused by Windows, stopped, error). Sent only with `on` true and `held` false; the hub keeps 40 characters and shows it in Health's hover.

caps.description: What this worker.py fully supports, also in its claim body. `challenger`: challenger / greedy jobs, their POST jobs/<lease>/watch preemption and stt_models.try (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py CAPS). `challenger_same_model`: a try id that this worker also serves live (its primary, a wanted model) runs on a separate try instance of the same files, never on the live server. The hub sends challenger jobs only to a worker whose latest hello, state or claim said it; a worker from before sends none. A hub from before ignores it.

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.description: A GPU worker's llama.cpp and whisper.cpp builds (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py Runtimes): the worker keeps the programs its servers run at the builds its worker.py pins (pins.json), downloading, testing and switching them itself, with a rollback. Only the runtimes its worker.toml runs; left out by a worker from before. The hub keeps it as said (sizeup/cloud/sttworkers.py clean_runtimes) and Health shows it on the worker's row. A hub from before ignores it.

llama.description: llama.cpp's llama-server (the local LLM, the Qwen3-ASR models).

whisper.description: whisper.cpp's whisper-server (worker.toml's whisper_server, the whisper models).

self_update.title: Self-update
self_update.description: A GPU worker's self-update (deploy/stt-worker/worker.py Updater): the worker.py it runs and what its updater is doing. Sending it is the capability: the hub answers `worker_update` only to a worker that sent it. A station's whisper never sends it.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the worker.py it runs, lower-case hex ("" when it can't read its file).

commit.description: The commit that file came from when the worker knows it (it updated itself to it), else "".

auto.description: auto_update in its config: false, it never updates itself.

state.description: The updater's state in words (current, staged, refused, rolled back, ...). The hub keeps 80 characters and shows it.

bad.description: Hashes it rolled back from and won't take again (the last 5).
